finding.claim: The WM_COPYDATA fallback reader accumulates an attacker-declared frame without any upper bound on the length prefix, so a peer can grow the client's buffer up to 4 GiB by streaming bytes. Impact is client memory exhaustion (availability only), and the path is narrow.
finding.source: Bytes written into PageantStream by the consumer. With SSH agent forwarding that is the remote SSH peer, relayed through the local client. The 4-byte big-endian length prefix is attacker-chosen (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFF).
finding.sink: BytesMut growth in the spawned reader task via two.read_buf(&mut buf) (wmmessage.rs:36) while the code waits for buf.len() >= len + 4 (wmmessage.rs:44).

trace.note: PageantStream::new() creates the duplex pair and spawns the reader task.
tokio::io::duplex capacity is 8192*100 bytes; it does not bound the BytesMut that the task drains into.
Task loops on read_buf, appending every received byte to buf with no cap.
len = BigEndian::read_u32(&buf) as usize, taken directly from the attacker-controlled prefix.
if buf.len() < len + 4 { continue; } keeps accumulating until the full claimed frame has arrived. No check that len <= _AGENT_MAX_MSGLEN happens here.
The only 8192-byte limit (MemoryMap::write) runs later, after the full frame has already been buffered.
Reachability: the named-pipe transport is tried first; this WM_COPYDATA path is used only when the pipe connection fails (lib.rs:38-48).

finding.guards_checked: buf.len() < 4 guard (wmmessage.rs:40); duplex capacity (wmmessage.rs:31); MemoryMap::write bounds check (wmmessage.rs:140-142) and MemoryMap::read bounds check (wmmessage.rs:161), which only run after full accumulation; _AGENT_MAX_MSGLEN constant (interface.rs:195). None of them caps len before the buffer grows. Reachability: narrow, because the named-pipe path (namedpipes.rs) is preferred and this path needs the WM_COPYDATA fallback.

finding.claim: The reader handles only one complete frame per read_buf wake-up. A second complete frame already sitting in buf is not processed until more bytes arrive, so a client that pipelines requests stalls waiting for a response that never comes. This is a logic flaw with mainly self-inflicted availability impact.
finding.source: A client (or a remote peer via agent forwarding) writing two or more agent request frames in one burst.
finding.sink: The loop returns to read_buf at wmmessage.rs:36 after processing a single split_to at wmmessage.rs:47 and the write at wmmessage.rs:54, instead of draining every complete frame already in buf.

trace.note: read_buf fills buf with two complete frames in one call.
split_to removes only the first frame; the second remains in buf.
The first response is written back, then control returns to the loop.
read_buf blocks waiting for new bytes even though a complete second frame is already buffered, so the second request is never answered.

finding.guards_checked: Frame-completeness check (wmmessage.rs:44) is correct for a single frame. The stall is that no inner loop processes further buffered frames before the next read.
